title: Diagnosis & Treatment of Foamy Urine | Dr. Vikas Jain
description: The diagnosis of foamy urine is done by a routine urine examination. It gives a clue for an underline problem for foamy urine. Treatment of foamy urine is based on underlying causes like urinary tract infections, proteinuria, and the presence of crystals.  Dr. Vikas Jain, Senior Consultant & Director – Urology and Renal Transplant at Narayana Superspeciality Hospital, Gurugram shared detailed information about the diagnosis & treatment of foamy urine.  #NarayanaHealth #HealthForAll #AllForHealth #NHCares  For video consultation with the doctor, log on to https://bit.ly/2z7Y0Bd  Visit our website https://www.narayanahealth.org to know more about Narayana Health and its facilities.  Connect with us:  Facebook - https://www.facebook.com/NarayanaHealth/ Instagram - https://www.instagram.com/narayanahealthindia/ Twitter - https://twitter.com/narayanahealth Blog - https://www.narayanahealth.org/blog/ LinkedIn - https://www.linkedin.com/company/narayanahealth

asr.full_text: Vekas Jain and kidney transplant results Good Morning. I am Doctor Vekas Jain. I am Director and Senior Consultant Department of Urology and kidney transplant from Narayana Super Specialty Hospital, Gurugram. Diagnosis of Femurian is very simple and can be done very easily with the help of Urine Routine Examination Urine Routine examination will give us a lot of clue what is the underlying problem for foaming urine If the urine shows pus cells that means the patient has got underlying urinary tract infection If the urine shows underlying proteins, or the proteins are excreted in larger amount, then it means the patient has got proteinuria and has got underlying problems like glomerulonephritis, diabetic proteinuria or even hypertension, as I told earlier. And the presence of crystals in the urine will point towards any stone in the genital urine tract which needs a detailed evaluation. diagnosis is very simple and simple urine examination gives us a lot of clue now coming to the treatment of forming urine the treatment depends on the underlying cause coming to the first cause that i mentioned that is a urinary tract infection urinary tract infection the urine will show us cells and on further evaluation if you do urine culture that you know and and appropriate antibiotics can be given to control or cure this problem however the patient will come back again with recurrent UTI what is the problem with that patient? and this will require a detailed evaluation for example it is a child and in a child who is coming to us with recurrent UTI, and foamy urine. We should always evaluate for underlying congenital abnormalities, if the child is harboring it, because many of these congenital abnormalities would present a recurrent UTI. If it is an adult female who is coming to us with recurrent UTI, we have to find out what is the cause of the recurrent UTI, whether she has got poor hygiene which she should be advised to take care of so if they take care of their personal hygiene properly, recurrent UTI can be prevented in a female. Now coming to adults, elderly males who have got underlying prosthetic problems and which is the actual cause of their recurrent UTI. So if we keep giving Antibiotics to treat their UTI and does not look after the prostate well they will come back to recurrent UTI sometimes these patients on detailed evaluation require a surgical intervention to take care of their prostate so that the recurrent UTI does not happen and the homine urine doesn't form., these are the problems and these are the treatment options in each age group for recurrent UTI. Coming to the second part of this, that is the Proteinuria. As I mentioned, Proteinuria can be because of the underlying glomerular disease, underlying diabetic glomerulopathies and can also be due to hypertension. So, if the patient has got glomerular disease, this requires a detailed evaluation. In this, you will find that urine also shows some sediments, it may be the same as the type of urine used by the patient as the patient may refer to a nephrologist and the patient may require a kidney biopsy to find out what is the type of underlying gloerose nephritis and they can be treated appropriately with the appropriate medicines which are available to us. The second cause of diabetes is Glaucoma allopathy. It is a very common problem. Most of the diabeties, who have got long-standing and uncontrolled diabetes, will come to us with proteinuria and Fomy urine. These patients need a need and aggressive control of their diabetes, they should change their lifestyle so their diabetes gets well controlled. So if a patient has got crystals in the urine, he may be harboring underlying stone disease anywhere in the genitourinary tract. By genitourinary tract I mean from kidney, ureter, and bladder. So if the patient has got this underlying stone disease, this needs an evaluation and these strains are larger in size, and if they are causing any obstruction to the urinary tract, they will require surgical intervention to remove. Now the surgical interventions are done in different ways and most of the interventions are minimally invasive and they do not require any big scars or cuts.
